/use-cases/create-invoice-in-claude/.intro: You want an invoice you can send today, not a table to copy into Word. Claude on its own stops short of that. The Invoice server gives you a numbered A4 PDF that keeps counting from the last one.
/use-cases/create-invoice-in-claude/.without_tool: Claude can lay out an invoice as text or a table and do the VAT math correctly. In Claude.ai with file creation turned on, it can also make a one-off PDF in its sandbox. It can't remember your last invoice number between chats, so numbering repeats or skips, and it keeps no list of what is paid or overdue.
/use-cases/create-invoice-in-claude/.with_tool: The Invoice server stores your business profile and clients, gives each invoice the next number that's never reused, and writes an A4 PDF with the VAT breakdown. It also records payments and lists what's overdue. With the local install the PDF is saved in a folder on your machine. On the hosted URL you get a short-lived download link.

example.prompt: Set my business details: Lens & Light, VAT GB123456789, IBAN on file. Then invoice the Harper family for one wedding day at GBP 1,600 and a print album at GBP 240, 20% VAT, due in 7 days, and give me the PDF.

steps.does: Saves the name, VAT id and bank details printed on every invoice
Stores the Harper family as a client
Makes the next invoice number with two lines and 20% VAT
Writes the A4 PDF and returns the path

example.result: A numbered A4 invoice for GBP 2,208.00 (GBP 1,840.00 net plus GBP 368.00 VAT), with bank details and a due date 7 days out.

pitfalls: Reusing or skipping invoice numbers when invoices are made in separate chats or files. Tax offices expect one unbroken sequence.
Leaving out your VAT id or the client's address, which makes the invoice invalid for VAT in many countries.
Sending the invoice and never recording the payment, so you can't tell later what's overdue.
/use-cases/create-invoice-in-claude/.answer: Claude can write invoice text and do the math, but it keeps no numbering or payment history between chats. Connect the Invoice server and Claude stores your clients, numbers each invoice in sequence, and writes an A4 PDF with VAT lines. The free tier works with no key. Pro removes the limits.

/use-cases/send-a-quote-from-chat/.intro: A quote stuck in a chat window doesn't win work. Freelancers and small firms need to price a job from their own price list, send a clean PDF and turn it into an invoice when the client says yes. Here's how.
/use-cases/send-a-quote-from-chat/.without_tool: Claude can draft quote wording, total the lines and add VAT. It doesn't know your current prices unless you paste them every time, it can't track which quotes are open, expired or accepted, and it can't hand an accepted quote to your invoicing.
/use-cases/send-a-quote-from-chat/.with_tool: Quotes stores each quote with a number, validity date and state, and writes an A4 PDF or a plain-text version for email. Catalogue keeps your SKUs and hourly rates with dates, so lines resolve to the price in force. quote_accept turns an accepted quote into an invoice in the Invoice server.

example.prompt: Quote the Okafor family: 6 m of worktop (SKU WT-OAK), 2 days of fitter time and 1 sink cut-out, prices from my catalogue, valid 30 days. Give me the PDF.

steps.does: Turns the SKU and role lines into priced items from the catalogue
Makes the quote with a number and a 30-day validity
Writes the A4 quote PDF

example.result: A numbered A4 quote priced from the stored catalogue, valid for 30 days, ready to attach to an email.

pitfalls: Quoting from memory and using last year's prices.
No expiry date, so a client accepts an old price months later.
Retyping an accepted quote as an invoice and making a typo in the amount.
/use-cases/send-a-quote-from-chat/.answer: Yes, with a quote server connected. On its own, Claude drafts quote text but can't store prices or quote states. The Quotes and Catalogue servers price lines from your list, number the quote, write a PDF, and turn an accepted quote into an invoice. Start on the free tier.

/use-cases/chase-overdue-invoices/.intro: Late payers are the most common cash problem in a small business. So you need three things: who to chase today, the right letter for how late they are, and a statement showing every open invoice.
/use-cases/chase-overdue-invoices/.without_tool: Claude writes a polite or firm reminder well if you give it the facts. It doesn't know which invoices are late today, what you already sent, or how much was part-paid. You have to keep that list yourself and paste it in each time.
/use-cases/chase-overdue-invoices/.with_tool: Dunning Letters keeps each unpaid invoice, records part payments and letters sent, and tells you which invoices cross a stage today. Statement of Account builds a per-client statement with aging buckets and writes it as an A4 PDF or email text.

example.persona: Office manager at an IT support firm
example.prompt: Make a statement of account for Brightwater Dental for September and October, with aging, as a PDF. Then write a firm chaser for everything they owe that's overdue.

steps.does: Builds the statement: opening balance, invoices, payments, closing balance
Writes the A4 statement of account
Writes a level 2 (firm) chaser that lists every overdue invoice

example.result: An A4 statement for Brightwater Dental with 0-30, 31-60 and 61-90 day buckets, plus a firm email that names each overdue invoice and the total due.

pitfalls: Sending the same friendly reminder at 60 days late as at 7 days late.
Chasing an invoice that was already part-paid, which annoys a client who did pay.
Chasing invoice by invoice instead of sending one statement with the full balance.
/use-cases/chase-overdue-invoices/.answer: Claude can write good reminder letters, but it can't see who is late today. Connect Dunning Letters to keep the chase list and letter stages, and Statement of Account to send a per-client statement PDF with aging. Both have a free tier with no key.

/use-cases/categorize-bank-statement/.intro: A month of bank lines needs categories before the accountant asks. Claude can sort a pasted statement once. Store the lines with rules and next month sorts itself.
/use-cases/categorize-bank-statement/.without_tool: Paste a CSV into Claude and it will suggest a category for each line in that chat. Long statements can hit the context limit, the categories aren't saved, and next month you start again with no rules and no history to compare.
/use-cases/categorize-bank-statement/.with_tool: Bank Statement imports the bank CSV into a stored ledger, applies your category rules to every line, and lets you set one-off categories by id. It finds recurring charges, summarizes spend by category and month, and exports a CSV or JSON file for your accountant.

example.prompt: Import my Revolut Business CSV for Q3. Put anything with 'Makro' under stock, 'Uber Eats' under platform fees, then give me spend per category per month and export it for my accountant.

steps.does: Reads the CSV and detects the columns
Stores the two match rules and applies them
Totals spend per category per month
Writes the categorized lines to a CSV file

example.result: Q3 spend grouped by category and month, plus a categorized CSV file the accountant can import.

pitfalls: Categorizing by hand every month instead of writing rules once.
Mixing personal and business accounts in one import, so totals are wrong.
Exporting before checking the uncategorized lines, which then end up as 'other'.
/use-cases/categorize-bank-statement/.answer: Claude can suggest categories for a pasted statement, but it saves nothing. With the Bank Statement server, Claude imports the CSV, applies saved rules to every line, finds recurring charges and exports a categorized file for your accountant. Next month the same rules run again.

/use-cases/track-billable-time-in-claude.intro: If you bill by the hour, lost minutes are lost income. Freelancers and consultants can start and stop a timer in the same chat where they work, then get invoice lines at the end of the week.
/use-cases/track-billable-time-in-claude.without_tool: Claude can't run a clock. It has no memory of when you started, and it can't keep a timesheet between chats. It can only add up hours you type in yourself.
/use-cases/track-billable-time-in-claude.with_tool: Time Tracker runs one stopwatch, logs entries with project, task and rate, and reports hours and money per period. It turns billable time into invoice lines, marks hours as billed so they aren't billed twice, and exports the timesheet to CSV.

example.prompt: I forgot to log yesterday: 2.5 hours on the Kowalski contract translation, billable, 160 PLN an hour. Then show this week's billable hours per project.

steps.does: Sets 160 PLN an hour for the Kowalski project
Logs 2.5 hours for yesterday and returns the amount
Totals this week's billable hours and money per project

example.result: A logged entry worth 400 PLN and a weekly table of billable hours and amounts per project.

pitfalls: Logging time from memory at the end of the week and losing 10-20% of it.
Billing the same hours twice because nothing marks them as invoiced.
One rate for every client when the contracts say otherwise.
/use-cases/track-billable-time-in-claude.answer: Claude has no clock, so it can't track time on its own. With the Time Tracker server, you say 'start a timer on project X' and 'stop', and Claude logs entries, totals billable hours per project and turns them into invoice lines. A CSV export is included.

/use-cases/log-expenses-and-receipts/.intro: Receipts get lost, and you can't reclaim VAT you can't prove. Sole traders and small teams do better logging each expense the moment it happens, with the receipt attached and the VAT already split.
/use-cases/log-expenses-and-receipts/.without_tool: Claude can read a receipt photo and tell you the merchant, amount and VAT. It doesn't keep a ledger, so each expense lives only in that chat. There's no running total, no project tag that lasts, and no export at month end.
/use-cases/log-expenses-and-receipts/.with_tool: Expense Tracker stores each expense with its net and VAT split, category, merchant and project, attaches the receipt file, and totals by category, project or month. It exports to CSV, XLSX or JSON, and turns billable expenses into invoice lines.

example.prompt: Log EUR 96.80 at Metro for table linen, 21% VAT, project Van Dijk wedding, billable. Attach receipt.jpg. Then export all October expenses to Excel.

steps.does: Records the expense with its net/VAT split and billable flag
Attaches receipt.jpg to that expense
Writes October's expenses to an .xlsx file

example.result: One stored expense (EUR 80.00 net, EUR 16.80 VAT) with its receipt, and an October .xlsx file for the accountant.

pitfalls: Recording the gross amount and forgetting to split out VAT.
Not tagging billable expenses to a project, so they never get rebilled.
Keeping receipt photos in the camera roll with no link to the entry.
/use-cases/log-expenses-and-receipts/.answer: Claude can read a receipt, but it keeps no ledger. Connect the Expense Tracker server and Claude stores each expense with its VAT split and project, attaches the receipt, totals by category and exports CSV or Excel at month end. Billable costs become invoice lines.

/use-cases/mileage-log-for-taxes/.intro: Tax offices want a mileage log made at the time of the trip, with date, route, distance and purpose. Drivers, trades and consultants can log each trip in one sentence. The deductible total is ready at year end.
/use-cases/mileage-log-for-taxes/.without_tool: Claude can multiply miles by a rate and write a log table if you list every trip. It doesn't keep the log between chats, it doesn't know which rate applied on which date, and it can't give you one file for the whole year.
/use-cases/mileage-log-for-taxes/.with_tool: Mileage Log stores each trip with an id, date, route, distance and category, keeps rates per jurisdiction with the date each one starts, and gives the deductible total per category. It exports the whole log as CSV.

example.prompt: Log three trips today: home to Oak Street 6.2 miles, Oak Street to Bay Road 4.8 miles, Bay Road to home 9.1 miles, all business. What's my deductible mileage for October?

steps.does: Logs each of the three trips with its own id
Totals October's business miles and the deductible amount at the stored rate

example.result: Three dated trip records (20.1 miles today) and October's deductible total at the rate on file.

pitfalls: Rebuilding the log from memory at tax time, which an auditor may not accept.
Using one rate for the whole year when the rate changed mid-year.
Logging the commute from home to a regular workplace as business mileage.
/use-cases/mileage-log-for-taxes/.answer: Claude can do mileage math, but it can't keep a log across the year. The Mileage Log server stores every trip with date, route and purpose, applies the rate in force on each date, and gives the deductible total and a CSV for your tax return.

/use-cases/merge-pdf-in-claude/.intro: You need one PDF out of several, or three PDFs out of one. And you don't want client documents on a random website. Below is what Claude can and can't do with PDFs, and how the PDF server writes the new file.
/use-cases/merge-pdf-in-claude/.without_tool: Claude can read the text of a PDF you attach and summarize it. In Claude.ai with code execution and file creation turned on, it can sometimes merge files in its sandbox. In Claude Desktop, Cursor or a plain chat, it can't write a new PDF.
/use-cases/merge-pdf-in-claude/.with_tool: The PDF server merges, splits, pulls pages, reorders, rotates, stamps words like PAID, and adds your business footer, each time writing a new PDF and returning the path. With the local install (npx or .mcpb) the files stay in your folders. On the hosted URL the files pass through the server for a short time.

example.prompt: Make one PDF from payslip-aug.pdf, payslip-sep.pdf, reference.pdf and id-scan.pdf in that order, but only page 1 of reference.pdf. Tell me the page count.

steps.does: Pulls page 1 of reference.pdf into a new file
Joins the four files in the given order
Reports the page count of the result

example.result: One application PDF in the order the letting agent asked for, with its page count.

pitfalls: Uploading contracts or ID scans to free online merge sites.
Merging in the wrong order and sending a pack that starts with page 3.
Rotating a scan in a viewer, which doesn't save the rotation in the file.
/use-cases/merge-pdf-in-claude/.answer: Claude can read PDFs, but in most chat apps it can't write a new one. Connect the PDF server and Claude merges, splits, reorders, rotates and stamps PDFs and returns the new file. Run it locally with npx if the files must stay on your machine.

/use-cases/create-word-document-in-claud.intro: Clients still want a .docx they can edit and track changes in. If you draft in Claude and then spend 20 minutes pasting into Word and fixing headings, read on.
/use-cases/create-word-document-in-claud.without_tool: Claude writes the content well. In Claude.ai with file creation turned on it can generate a .docx in its sandbox. In Claude Desktop, Cursor or apps without that feature, you get text to copy and format by hand, and it can't fill your own .docx template.
/use-cases/create-word-document-in-claud.with_tool: The DOCX server writes real .docx files from sections or markdown, fills {{placeholders}} in your own template, reads existing .docx files, and makes proposals and service agreements with your stored sender details.

example.prompt: Turn these meeting notes into a Word document with the heading 'Volunteer Day Plan', a section per team and a table of shift times.

steps.does: Turns the structured notes into a .docx and counts the headings, tables and paragraphs

example.result: A .docx with one heading per team and a shift table, ready to share and edit in Word or Google Docs.

pitfalls: Pasting from chat into Word and losing the heading styles, so there's no navigation pane.
Retyping a standard letter instead of filling a template.
Sending a .docx with leftover {{placeholders}} because nobody checked.
/use-cases/create-word-document-in-claud.answer: Yes. Claude.ai can make a .docx when file creation is on. Other chat apps give you text only. The DOCX server works in any MCP client: it writes .docx files from markdown, fills your own templates and reads existing documents. Free tier first.

/use-cases/edit-excel-files-in-claude/.intro: Most small business data lives in .xlsx and .csv files. You want answers from a spreadsheet in plain words, and a new file with the change made. No formulas.
/use-cases/edit-excel-files-in-claude/.without_tool: In Claude.ai with code execution, Claude can analyze an uploaded spreadsheet and create a new one. In Claude Desktop or Cursor without a tool, it can't open a file path on your disk, and large files may not fit in the chat.
/use-cases/edit-excel-files-in-claude/.with_tool: The Spreadsheet server reads, queries, searches and summarizes .xlsx and .csv files by path, adds computed columns and converts between xlsx, csv and json. Every change is written to a new file. The source file isn't changed.

example.prompt: Open ~/Downloads/orders_export.csv. Which 10 products sold the most units in October? Save that list as top-products.xlsx.

steps.does: Reads the columns and row count
Filters October, groups by product, sorts by units
Writes the top 10 rows to top-products.xlsx

example.result: A ranked top-10 list in chat and a new top-products.xlsx file. The original export is unchanged.

pitfalls: Editing the only copy of a file and losing the original data.
Treating dates stored as text as real dates, so filters miss rows.
Asking for totals on a column that mixes currencies.
/use-cases/edit-excel-files-in-claude/.answer: Claude.ai can analyze spreadsheets with code execution. To work with .xlsx and .csv files by path in Claude Desktop, Cursor or VS Code, connect the Spreadsheet server: it reads, queries, adds columns and converts, and writes each result to a new file.

/use-cases/three-way-match-invoices/.intro: Paying for goods that never arrived is expensive. AP clerks and controllers check each invoice line against the purchase order and the goods receipt before payment. A server can do that check line by line.
/use-cases/three-way-match-invoices/.without_tool: Claude can compare three documents you paste and point out differences. It can miss a mistake when two SKU errors cancel out and the totals agree, it doesn't know what was invoiced before, and it keeps no record of the check.
/use-cases/three-way-match-invoices/.with_tool: Three-Way Match compares each SKU, unit price and billed quantity with the PO, all accepted deliveries, and quantities already invoiced, and returns every exception with the source values. Goods Receipt stores POs and GRNs with damage and shortage. Three-Way Match runs locally. You give it structured data, not PDFs.

example.persona: AP clerk at a food distributor
example.prompt: Record PO-7781 for 200 cases of tinned tomatoes, then a goods receipt with 180 cases accepted and 4 damaged. List the discrepancies before I match the invoice.

steps.does: Creates the purchase order with its line
Records the receipt: 180 accepted, 4 damaged
Lists the short and damaged lines
Checks the supplier invoice against the PO and accepted quantity

example.result: A discrepancy list showing 20 cases short and 4 damaged, and a match report that flags any invoice line billed above the accepted quantity.

pitfalls: Matching on invoice total only, which hides offsetting line errors.
Forgetting earlier partial invoices on the same PO, so the quantity gets paid twice.
Booking damaged goods as received in full.
/use-cases/three-way-match-invoices/.answer: Claude can compare documents you paste, but totals can hide line errors. The Three-Way Match server checks every SKU, price and quantity against the PO, accepted receipts and earlier invoices, and returns each exception with its source. It runs locally and doesn't read PDFs.

/use-cases/find-duplicate-invoices/.intro: Duplicate supplier invoices are one of the most common ways money leaks out of accounts payable. Bookkeepers and AP teams can check a payment run before it goes to the bank.
/use-cases/find-duplicate-invoices/.without_tool: Claude can scan a short pasted list and spot obvious repeats. On a few hundred rows it can miss near-repeats, it can't save the result as evidence, and it gives no CSV you can attach to the approval.
/use-cases/find-duplicate-invoices/.with_tool: Duplicate Invoice Check takes a batch of invoice records, returns candidate duplicate groups with the reason for each, saves the report and exports it as CSV. It runs locally from a source checkout. It doesn't read PDFs or approve payment.

example.prompt: Check these 85 invoices from the Hartley Builders AP export for duplicates before Thursday's payment run, and give me the CSV.

steps.does: Groups invoices that look like the same bill and states why
Exports the saved report as CSV

example.result: A list of candidate duplicate groups with reasons, and a CSV to attach to the payment approval.

pitfalls: Checking only exact invoice numbers, when duplicates often differ by a dash or a prefix.
Running the check after the payment run instead of before.
Deleting the suspected duplicate without asking the supplier which one is real.
/use-cases/find-duplicate-invoices/.answer: Claude can spot obvious repeats in a short list, but it saves no evidence. The Duplicate Invoice Check server scans a whole batch, groups candidate duplicates with a reason for each, and exports a CSV for the approver. It runs locally. It doesn't approve or block payments.

/use-cases/reconcile-supplier-statement/.intro: Every month a supplier sends a statement that doesn't agree with your ledger. Before you call them, you want to know exactly which items differ, and why.
/use-cases/reconcile-supplier-statement/.without_tool: Claude can compare two short lists you paste and find some differences. With 40 or more open items it can lose track, it doesn't keep the result, and it can't give you a CSV of the differences.
/use-cases/reconcile-supplier-statement/.with_tool: Supplier Statement Check compares the supplier's statement with your open items at a date, lists each difference with the source values, saves the report and exports CSV. It runs only as a local install from a source checkout. It doesn't read PDFs or post payments.

example.persona: Accounts assistant at a print shop
example.prompt: Here is the statement from Northern Paper Co at 31 October (28 lines) and our open items for them. What doesn't agree?

steps.does: Compares the two sides and lists every difference
Shows the detail for each mismatched item

example.result: A list of items only on the supplier side, items only on yours, and amount differences, with the values behind each.

pitfalls: Comparing only balances, so you know the gap but not which invoice causes it.
Ignoring timing: a payment sent on the 30th that the supplier books on the 2nd.
Paying the statement balance without checking it.
/use-cases/reconcile-supplier-statement/.answer: Claude can compare short lists, but long statements need a tool. The Supplier Statement Check server matches the supplier's statement against your open items, lists every difference with its source values, and exports a CSV. It runs as a local install only and needs structured data, not PDF scans.

/use-cases/depreciation-schedule/.intro: Most small businesses hand depreciation to the accountant because the schedule is tedious, not hard. One sentence per asset gets you the schedule and the monthly journal.
/use-cases/depreciation-schedule/.without_tool: Claude knows the straight-line and declining-balance methods and can build a schedule for one asset in a chat. It doesn't keep a register, so next month it doesn't know what you own, what's fully written down, or what was sold.
/use-cases/depreciation-schedule/.with_tool: Asset Register stores each fixed asset with cost, method, rate and life, builds the schedule, gives the monthly journal (debit depreciation expense, credit accumulated depreciation), records disposals with gain or loss, and reports net book value for the year.

example.persona: Owner of a small dental lab
example.prompt: Add a milling machine bought 1 April 2026 for EUR 42,000, straight line over 7 years. Show me its schedule and the net book value at 31 December.

steps.does: Adds the machine to the register with its method and life
Builds the year-by-year schedule
Shows net book value at 31 December

example.result: A 7-year schedule and the net book value at year end. The machine stays in the register for next month's journal.

pitfalls: Starting depreciation from the wrong date (purchase date vs date in use).
Forgetting to remove a sold asset, so it keeps depreciating on paper.
Mixing the tax method and the book method in one schedule.
/use-cases/depreciation-schedule/.answer: Claude can explain and calculate depreciation for one asset, but it keeps no register. The Asset Register server stores your assets, builds schedules, gives the monthly journal and records disposals. Check the method and rates with your accountant. The server applies what you set.

/use-cases/loan-and-lease-amortization/.intro: Owners and accountants need three things for a loan or lease. A payment schedule, the interest and principal split of each payment, and the journal entries that go with it.
/use-cases/loan-and-lease-amortization/.without_tool: Claude can compute a level payment and a schedule for one loan if the inputs are clear, and it's usually right. It keeps no register of your loans, so it can't tell you next month what's outstanding across all of them.
/use-cases/loan-and-lease-amortization/.with_tool: Amortization stores each loan or lease, builds the schedule per period, gives the journal entry for any period or month, prices early repayment, and reports total debt outstanding at a date.

example.persona: Bakery owner buying an oven on finance
example.prompt: Record an equipment loan: EUR 18,000 at 7.5% a year over 48 months. What's the monthly payment, and how much interest do I pay in 2027?

steps.does: Records the loan and returns the level monthly payment
Builds the schedule with interest and principal per month

example.result: The monthly payment, a 48-row schedule, and the 2027 interest total read from it.

pitfalls: Booking the full payment as an expense instead of splitting interest and principal.
Comparing offers on the nominal rate instead of the effective annual rate.
Forgetting the early repayment fee when deciding to overpay.
/use-cases/loan-and-lease-amortization/.answer: Claude can calculate a loan payment, but it keeps no record of your loans. With the Amortization server, Claude stores each loan or lease, builds the full schedule, gives the interest and principal journal per month and prices early repayment.

/use-cases/per-diem-travel-allowance/.intro: Per diem rules differ by country, scheme and trip length. Get them wrong and you over- or under-pay staff. Ops and finance teams need the right daily allowance for a trip and an expense line to match.
/use-cases/per-diem-travel-allowance/.without_tool: Claude can explain how a per diem scheme works, but its rates may be out of date and it may not cite the source. It doesn't save trips, so there's no monthly total per scheme.
/use-cases/per-diem-travel-allowance/.with_tool: Per Diem calculates the allowance for a trip from bundled scheme rates and lists each rate with its authority and source URL. It saves trips, reports monthly totals per scheme, and returns the exact expense_add arguments for the Expense Tracker.

example.persona: Office manager at an engineering firm
example.prompt: Which per diem schemes and rates do you have? Then save a trip for Maria: Warsaw to Prague, 3 to 5 November, and give me the expense lines.

steps.does: Lists the bundled schemes with authority and source URL
Calculates the trip and saves it
Returns the expense_add arguments for the trip

example.result: The saved trip with its daily allowance and total, plus expense lines ready for the Expense Tracker.

pitfalls: Using last year's rates.
Paying full days for partial travel days when the scheme pays less.
Forgetting to reduce the allowance when meals were provided.
/use-cases/per-diem-travel-allowance/.answer: Claude can explain per diem rules, but its rates may be out of date. The Per Diem server calculates the allowance from bundled scheme rates that list their source, saves each trip and returns expense lines. Check the scheme list first. If your scheme is missing, the server can't calculate it.

/use-cases/work-orders-and-job-cards/.intro: Trades and field service crews lose money when parts and hours never make it onto the invoice. Plumbers, electricians and maintenance firms can raise a job, log what was used and bill it from the van.
/use-cases/work-orders-and-job-cards/.without_tool: Claude can write a work order or job sheet as text. It doesn't number jobs, it can't track a job from scheduled to done to invoiced, and it forgets the parts and hours logged in an earlier chat.
/use-cases/work-orders-and-job-cards/.with_tool: Work Order raises numbered jobs, adds parts and labour lines, moves each job through its status, writes an A4 completion report PDF, and builds an invoice payload. Job Card logs labour by worker and day, logs materials, and prints a card for the client.

example.prompt: Open a job card for the Reyes house, rewire the kitchen. Log 6 hours for Tom and 6 for Ana today at 45 an hour, and 30 m of 2.5 mm cable at 1.20 a metre. Print the card.

steps.does: Opens a numbered job card for the Reyes kitchen
Logs 6 hours each for Tom and Ana
Logs 30 m of cable
Renders the card with labour, materials and total

example.result: A printable job card: 12 hours of labour (540), 30 m of cable (36), total 576 before tax.

pitfalls: Writing parts on paper and forgetting them at invoice time.
No status, so finished jobs sit unbilled for weeks.
Logging hours per job but not per worker, so payroll doesn't match.
/use-cases/work-orders-and-job-cards/.answer: Claude can draft a job sheet, but it doesn't number or track jobs. Connect Work Order and Job Card and Claude raises numbered jobs, logs labour and materials, moves each job to done and invoiced, and prints a completion report or job card.

/use-cases/change-orders/.intro: Scope creep without paperwork is unpaid work. Contractors and agencies need to record extra work against a quote, get the client to approve it and bill the difference.
/use-cases/change-orders/.without_tool: Claude can write a change order letter. It doesn't know the original quote value, it can't keep a running contract total across several changes, and it doesn't track which changes were approved.
/use-cases/change-orders/.with_tool: Change Order raises numbered change orders against a quote or work order, adds and removes lines, moves each one from draft to sent to approved, gives the running contract value, and builds invoice lines for the approved difference.

example.prompt: What's the contract value on quote Q-2026-022 now? Then raise a change order: remove the gravel path (EUR 1,100) and add a timber deck, EUR 3,400.

steps.does: Shows original value, approved changes and current value
Raises a numbered change order against Q-2026-022
Adds the deck and removes the path
Renders the change order for the client to approve

example.result: A numbered change order with a net increase of EUR 2,300 and a document for the client to approve.

pitfalls: Doing the extra work on a verbal yes, then arguing about it at the end.
Billing the full new scope instead of the difference.
Losing track of the current contract value after several changes.
/use-cases/change-orders/.answer: Claude can draft a change order letter, but it can't track contract value across changes. The Change Order server records each change against the quote, tracks approval, shows the running contract value and builds invoice lines for the approved difference.

/use-cases/purchase-orders-and-credit-no.intro: Small firms most often make purchase orders and credit notes by editing an old file. Both should be correct, numbered and linked to the right supplier or invoice.
/use-cases/purchase-orders-and-credit-no.without_tool: Claude can draft a purchase order or a credit note as text. It doesn't number them, it doesn't know the original invoice lines and VAT rates, and it can't track which orders have arrived.
/use-cases/purchase-orders-and-credit-no.with_tool: Billing Docs raises numbered purchase orders, records full or partial receipt, and credits an invoice in full, by amount or by line, writing A4 PDFs or email text. Credit Note issues standalone or invoice-linked credit notes and finalizes them with a CN number.

example.persona: Owner of a bike repair shop
example.prompt: A customer returned a helmet sold on INV-2026-0140. Issue a credit note for one helmet at EUR 59 incl. 21% VAT, reason 'returned unused', and finalize it.

steps.does: Creates a draft credit note linked to INV-2026-0140
Assigns the final CN number and freezes the note
Renders it to paste into an email

example.result: A finalized, numbered credit note for EUR 59.00 (EUR 48.76 net plus EUR 10.24 VAT) that names the original invoice.

pitfalls: Editing or deleting the original invoice instead of issuing a credit note.
Crediting the gross amount at the wrong VAT rate.
Sending a purchase order with no expected delivery date, so nobody chases it.
/use-cases/purchase-orders-and-credit-no.answer: Claude can draft the wording, but it doesn't number documents or know your invoice lines. Connect Billing Docs and Credit Note and Claude raises numbered purchase orders, records deliveries, and issues credit notes linked to the right invoice with correct VAT.

/use-cases/bill-of-sale/.intro: A bill of sale protects both sides when you sell a car, a boat, equipment or a business asset privately. Private sellers and small dealers can get a correct, signable document in a few minutes.
/use-cases/bill-of-sale/.without_tool: Claude can write a bill of sale from a template and include the usual fields. It keeps no record of past sales, can't freeze a final version, and leaves you to format and print it.
/use-cases/bill-of-sale/.with_tool: Bill of Sale records the seller, buyer, item and identifier (VIN or serial), price and terms, renders the document as Markdown or a printable HTML file, and freezes it when finalized. It keeps a book of every sale with totals.

example.prompt: Bill of sale: I, Dana Moore, sell a 2019 utility trailer, VIN 1UJBJ0BN8K1TS0000, to Luis Ortega for USD 2,350, sold as is, paid in cash today. Render it so I can print two copies.

steps.does: Records the sale with the VIN, price and as-is terms
Freezes the document for signing
Writes a printable HTML document

example.result: A finalized, printable bill of sale with both parties, the VIN, USD 2,350, 'as is' terms and signature lines.

pitfalls: Leaving out the VIN or serial number, so the document doesn't identify the item.
Not writing 'sold as is' when that's the deal.
Using a generic form when your state or country requires a specific one or a notary. Check local rules.
/use-cases/bill-of-sale/.answer: Claude can draft a bill of sale. The Bill of Sale server adds a numbered record, freezes the final version and renders a printable document with VIN or serial, price and terms. Some places require an official form or notary. Check local rules.

/use-cases/tailored-resume-and-cover-let.intro: Stop rewriting the same CV for every posting. Keep one profile, see the gaps against a specific job, and get a Word resume and cover letter out of chat.
/use-cases/tailored-resume-and-cover-let.without_tool: Claude is good at rewriting a CV for a job post you paste. It doesn't keep your profile between chats, so you paste the CV every time, and in most chat apps it gives you text, not a .docx you can send.
/use-cases/tailored-resume-and-cover-let.with_tool: Resume stores one CV profile, reads an existing .docx resume into it, runs a read-only gap analysis against a job posting, and writes the resume and cover letter as .docx files, or as HTML and markdown.

example.prompt: Here is a posting for Clinical Product Specialist. What in my profile matches, what's missing? Then write a cover letter .docx for it.

steps.does: Loads the stored CV profile
Lists matched and missing skills against the posting. Changes nothing
Writes a one-page cover letter .docx

example.result: A list of matched and missing requirements, and a one-page cover letter .docx built from the stored profile.

pitfalls: Sending one generic CV to every job.
Adding skills you don't have to match keywords. Interviews expose it.
Fancy layouts with tables and columns that some applicant tracking systems read badly.
/use-cases/tailored-resume-and-cover-let.answer: Claude rewrites CVs well, but it forgets your profile between chats. With the Resume server, Claude stores your profile once, shows the gaps against each job post and writes the resume and cover letter as Word files. The gap analysis changes nothing.

/use-cases/freelance-service-agreement/.intro: Most freelance payment disputes start with no written scope. Freelancers and small agencies need a service agreement with scope, rate, deliverables and the right clauses before work starts.
/use-cases/freelance-service-agreement/.without_tool: Claude can draft a service agreement and explain common clauses. It keeps no list of your agreements, can't reuse your own clause wording reliably, and doesn't check what's missing before you send. It isn't a lawyer, and neither is a tool.
/use-cases/freelance-service-agreement/.with_tool: Service Agreement writes numbered agreements with parties, scope, deliverables and rate, runs a before-you-send checklist, renders the document and tracks status from draft to signed. Clauses stores your own clause library and assembles contracts as .docx or markdown.

example.prompt: Agreement with Greenleaf Foods: 8 blog posts a month for 3 months at USD 2,400 a month, 2 revision rounds. What's missing before I send it?

steps.does: Writes the agreement with scope, rate and term
Lists missing fields and risky terms
Renders the agreement ready to send

example.result: A numbered service agreement for USD 7,200 over 3 months and a checklist of what to add before sending.

pitfalls: No limit on revisions, so the job never ends.
Not stating who owns the work until it's paid.
Starting work before the agreement is signed. Have a lawyer check terms that matter.
/use-cases/freelance-service-agreement/.answer: Claude can draft a contract, and the Service Agreement server adds structure: numbered agreements, a before-you-send checklist, your own clause library and status from draft to signed. Neither replaces legal advice. Have a lawyer check terms that carry real risk.

/use-cases/recurring-monthly-invoices/.intro: Retainers and subscriptions should bill themselves. If you send the same invoice every month and sometimes forget, this is for you.
/use-cases/recurring-monthly-invoices/.without_tool: Claude can't act on a schedule. It doesn't run on the 1st of the month, it doesn't know which periods were billed, and it can't create invoices in a system that keeps numbers.
/use-cases/recurring-monthly-invoices/.with_tool: Recurring stores schedules (client, lines, cadence, start and end), creates real invoices in the Invoice server for every due occurrence when you ask, keeps an audit log per schedule, and forecasts recurring revenue per month.

example.persona: IT support company with 12 retainer clients
example.prompt: Which retainer invoices fall due in the next 14 days? Skip November for Alder Law, they are closed that month. Then generate everything due today.

steps.does: Lists every occurrence due in the next 14 days
Closes the November occurrence for Alder Law
Creates a real invoice for every occurrence due today

example.result: A list of upcoming retainer invoices, one skipped period, and today's invoices created with their numbers in the Invoice server.

pitfalls: Assuming the chat app sends invoices on its own. You still ask it to generate due invoices.
Pausing a client and forgetting the missed periods are still due when you resume.
Changing the price in the invoice instead of the schedule, so next month is wrong again.
/use-cases/recurring-monthly-invoices/.answer: Claude can't run on a schedule by itself. With Recurring and Invoice connected, you ask once a week and Claude creates every invoice that's due, skips or pauses clients, keeps an audit log per schedule and forecasts your monthly recurring revenue.

/use-cases/sepa-payment-qr-code/.intro: In much of Europe a client can pay an invoice by scanning a QR code in their banking app. Euro-zone freelancers and firms can put that code on every invoice without a separate generator.
/use-cases/sepa-payment-qr-code/.without_tool: Claude can explain the EPC QR format and list the fields. It can't draw an image, so it can't make a code a banking app will scan.
/use-cases/sepa-payment-qr-code/.with_tool: Barcode makes an EPC069-12 SEPA payment QR code from IBAN, beneficiary, amount and reference, or one for a stored invoice using the IBAN from your business profile. It writes SVG or PNG and also makes plain QR, vCard, WiFi and linear barcodes.

example.prompt: Make a SEPA payment QR for EUR 3,630.00 to Studio Vos, IBAN NL91ABNA0417164300, reference 2026-118, as PNG.

steps.does: Encodes the payment as an EPC069-12 QR code and writes a PNG

example.result: A PNG payment QR code the client scans in their banking app to pay EUR 3,630.00 with reference 2026-118 filled in.

pitfalls: A typo in the IBAN. Always test-scan the code with your own banking app first.
Leaving out the reference, so the payment can't be matched to the invoice.
Using an EPC code for a non-euro payment. The standard is euro only.
/use-cases/sepa-payment-qr-code/.answer: Claude can't draw a scannable QR code by itself. The Barcode server makes an EPC069-12 SEPA payment QR from IBAN, name, amount and reference as SVG or PNG, so the client pays from their banking app. Test-scan it before you send.

/use-cases/schedule-across-time-zones/.intro: Remote teams lose hours to 'what time is that for you?'. Ops staff and assistants need a meeting time inside everyone's working hours, and a calendar file to send.
/use-cases/schedule-across-time-zones/.without_tool: Claude knows time zones, but it can get daylight saving dates wrong, especially in the weeks when the US and Europe change clocks on different days. It doesn't know your calendar or anyone's working hours.
/use-cases/schedule-across-time-zones/.with_tool: Timezone stores people with their zone and working hours, ranks meeting slots inside everyone's hours on real dates, lists clock changes and writes a .ics file. Calendar imports your .ics calendars, finds free and busy time, and flags double bookings.

example.prompt: Find a 30-minute slot next Tuesday for Priya in Bangalore, Tom in Chicago and me in Lisbon, inside working hours. Check my imported calendar is free, and make the .ics.

steps.does: Ranks times inside all three working days
Checks the slot against the imported calendar
Writes a .ics invite for the chosen slot

example.result: A ranked list of slots that fit all three days, a check against your calendar, and a .ics file to send.

pitfalls: Scheduling in the weeks when the US and Europe have changed clocks on different dates.
Picking a time that's inside working hours for two people and 7 am for the third.
Sending a time in your zone only, with no calendar file.
/use-cases/schedule-across-time-zones/.answer: Claude knows time zones, but daylight saving gaps trip it up and it can't see calendars. With Timezone and Calendar connected, Claude ranks slots inside everyone's working hours on real dates, checks your imported calendar for clashes and writes a .ics invite.

/use-cases/petty-cash-reconciliation/.intro: The petty cash tin never agrees with the book. Office managers and bookkeepers who run an imprest float want vouchers, a count and a top-up figure without a spreadsheet.
/use-cases/petty-cash-reconciliation/.without_tool: Claude can explain the imprest system and add up vouchers you type in. It doesn't keep the float, the voucher numbers or past counts, so each month starts from nothing.
/use-cases/petty-cash-reconciliation/.with_tool: Petty Cash opens a float, records numbered vouchers and top-ups, reconciles a cash count against the expected balance, and works out the top-up that restores the imprest.

example.persona: Office manager at a veterinary clinic
example.prompt: Add vouchers from the tin: GBP 12.40 milk and coffee, GBP 18.00 parking for the locum, GBP 7.99 batteries. I counted GBP 161.61. Does it reconcile against the GBP 200 float?

steps.does: Records each of the three vouchers with a number
Compares the count with the expected balance

example.result: Three numbered vouchers (GBP 38.39), an expected balance of GBP 161.61, and a reconciliation that agrees to the penny.

pitfalls: Taking cash out with no voucher, so the tin is always short.
Topping up to a round number instead of the exact amount spent.
Counting rarely, so a mistake from six weeks ago is impossible to trace.
/use-cases/petty-cash-reconciliation/.answer: Claude can explain petty cash, but it keeps no float or vouchers. The Petty Cash server records each voucher, reconciles your cash count against the expected balance, and calculates the top-up that restores the imprest. Each month continues from the last.

/use-cases/employee-leave-tracker/.intro: Small teams track leave in a shared spreadsheet until two people book the same week. Owners and HR staff want requests, approvals, balances and 'who is out' in one place they can ask in plain words.
/use-cases/employee-leave-tracker/.without_tool: Claude can calculate a leave balance from numbers you give it. It keeps no record of employees, requests or approvals, and it can't tell you who is out next week.
/use-cases/employee-leave-tracker/.with_tool: Leave stores employees with their allowance, creates and approves requests, shows each balance with carry-over and pending days, and lists who is out in a date range. Pro adds CSV import and an .ics export of approved leave.

example.prompt: Add Sam with 25 days a year. Sam asks for 2 to 6 November off as vacation. Approve it, and show Sam's balance.

steps.does: Adds Sam with 25 days of annual leave
Creates the vacation request
Approves the request
Shows allowance, used and remaining days

example.result: An approved request for 5 working days and Sam's balance: 20 days left.

pitfalls: Approving leave without checking who else is out that week.
Forgetting carry-over rules at year end.
Counting calendar days instead of working days.
/use-cases/employee-leave-tracker/.answer: Claude can do leave math, but it keeps no records. The Leave server stores employees and allowances, handles requests and approvals, shows each balance and lists who is out in any date range. Pro adds CSV import and calendar export.

/use-cases/new-hire-onboarding-plan/.intro: A new hire's first week sets how long they stay. Small business owners and HR staff need a plan with owners and due dates, and a quick way to see what's late.
/use-cases/new-hire-onboarding-plan/.without_tool: Claude can write a good onboarding plan for a role. It doesn't save it, assign tasks to owners with dates, or tell you next Friday which tasks are overdue.
/use-cases/new-hire-onboarding-plan/.with_tool: Onboarding adds hires, applies role templates, assigns tasks to HR, manager or IT with due dates, tracks progress and lists overdue tasks. Checklist runs reusable, versioned checklists with pass, fail and sign-off for first-day steps.

example.persona: Practice manager at a physiotherapy clinic
example.prompt: New hire: Leo Grant, receptionist, starts 17 November. Add tasks: IT sets up booking system login by the 14th, manager does a shadow shift on the 17th, HR collects right-to-work documents by the 17th. Show his plan.

steps.does: Adds Leo with role and start date
Adds each task with an owner and due date
Shows the whole plan with owners, dates and percent done

example.result: A plan for Leo with three owned, dated tasks, and a progress view you can check again before day one.

pitfalls: Accounts and equipment not ready on day one.
No owner per task, so everyone assumes someone else did it.
Skipping legal steps, such as right-to-work checks, in a busy week.
/use-cases/new-hire-onboarding-plan/.answer: Claude can draft an onboarding plan, but it can't track it. With the Onboarding server, Claude adds hires, assigns tasks to HR, managers or IT with due dates, applies role templates and lists overdue tasks. Checklist adds signed-off first-day checklists.

/use-cases/resize-and-compress-images/.intro: Your photos are too big for the website or the email. Shop owners and bloggers can resize, compress and convert a batch of images just by asking in chat.
/use-cases/resize-and-compress-images/.without_tool: Claude can look at an image and describe it. In Claude.ai with code execution it can sometimes resize a file in its sandbox. In Claude Desktop or Cursor without a tool, it can't write a new image file.
/use-cases/resize-and-compress-images/.with_tool: The Image server resizes single images or batches, compresses and reports bytes before and after, converts formats, crops, makes thumbnails, adds a text watermark and strips metadata. Each result is a new file.

example.prompt: Make 400 px thumbnails of every photo in ~/shop/new-mugs into ~/shop/thumbs, then tell me the size of the largest original.

steps.does: Writes one thumbnail per photo into the output folder
Reads format, pixel size and file size of the originals

example.result: A folder of 400 px thumbnails named <name>-thumb, and the size of the largest original photo.

pitfalls: Uploading full-size phone photos (4-8 MB) to a web shop, which slows every page.
Compressing a JPEG again and again, which adds visible artifacts.
Posting photos with GPS location still in the metadata.
/use-cases/resize-and-compress-images/.answer: In most chat apps Claude can see an image but not write a new one. The Image server resizes, compresses, converts, crops, watermarks and strips metadata, in batches, and writes each result as a new file. Run it locally to keep photos on your machine.

/use-cases/convert-currency-ecb-rates/.intro: Accountants and freelancers who invoice abroad need the official rate for a specific date, not a rate a chatbot remembers. If you must convert at the ECB reference rate and show where the number came from, start here.
/use-cases/convert-currency-ecb-rates/.without_tool: Claude has no live data in a plain chat. It may give a rate from its training data that's months old, and it can't prove which date the rate is from.
/use-cases/convert-currency-ecb-rates/.with_tool: Currency uses European Central Bank daily reference rates: it converts on a given date, converts one amount into many currencies, gives the rate for a pair on a date, and returns rate history for a window.

example.persona: UK freelancer billing a German client
example.prompt: What was the ECB EUR to GBP rate on 30 September 2026, and what's EUR 5,750 in GBP at that rate?

steps.does: Returns the ECB rate for EUR/GBP on that date, both directions
Converts EUR 5,750 at that date's rate

example.result: The ECB reference rate for 30 September 2026 and the GBP amount, with the rate date stated so it can be cited on the invoice.

pitfalls: Using today's rate for an invoice dated last month.
Using a bank's buy or sell rate where the tax office expects a reference rate.
Forgetting that ECB rates are published only on working days.
/use-cases/convert-currency-ecb-rates/.answer: Without a tool, Claude may quote an old rate from memory. The Currency server uses European Central Bank daily reference rates: it converts on any date, converts into many currencies at once and gives rate history, with the rate date stated.

/can-claude/create-excel-files/.intro: Sometimes. It depends on where you use Claude. Some Claude apps can make an .xlsx today, and Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code can get the same result with a server.
/can-claude/create-excel-files/.without_tool: In Claude.ai with code execution and file creation turned on, Claude can create .xlsx files in a sandbox and give you a download. In Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code without a tool, it gives you CSV or table text to paste, and it can't open a spreadsheet on your disk.
/can-claude/create-excel-files/.with_tool: The Spreadsheet server writes rows to .xlsx, .csv, .tsv or .json, reads and queries existing spreadsheets by path, adds computed columns and converts formats. Each change is a new file. The source isn't changed.

example.persona: Volunteer treasurer of a sports club
example.prompt: Make members-2026.xlsx with columns name, membership type, paid date and amount, from the list I paste below.

steps.does: Writes the rows to members-2026.xlsx
Summarizes the amount column: count, total, min, max

example.result: A real .xlsx file with the member list, and a summary of how much has been paid.

pitfalls: Copying a chat table into Excel and getting all values in one column.
Numbers saved as text, so totals don't work.
Expecting formulas to be kept when converting to CSV.
/can-claude/create-excel-files/.answer: Claude.ai can create Excel files when code execution and file creation are on. In Claude Desktop, Cursor or VS Code, connect the Spreadsheet server: Claude then writes .xlsx and .csv files, reads existing spreadsheets by path, adds columns and converts formats.

/can-claude/create-word-documents/.intro: Yes in Claude.ai with file creation on, and with a connected server everywhere else. Below is the difference, and what you can do with your own Word templates.
/can-claude/create-word-documents/.without_tool: In Claude.ai with file creation turned on, Claude can generate a .docx in its sandbox. In Claude Desktop, Cursor or VS Code without a tool, you get text to paste into Word, and Claude can't fill or read a .docx template on your disk.
/can-claude/create-word-documents/.with_tool: The DOCX server writes .docx files from sections or markdown, fills {{placeholders}} in your own template, reads existing .docx files, converts .docx to HTML and makes proposals and service agreements.

example.prompt: Fill parent-letter-template.docx: {{parent_name}} Mrs Ito, {{student}} Ken, {{trip_date}} 14 November, {{cost}} GBP 18. Save it as letter-ito.docx.

steps.does: Replaces each placeholder and reports any it couldn't fill

example.result: letter-ito.docx with the school's own layout and every placeholder filled, plus a report of any missing fields.

pitfalls: Expecting a chat answer to keep Word heading styles when pasted.
Placeholders that differ by one character, so they aren't replaced.
Starting from a blank document when the organization has a letterhead template.
/can-claude/create-word-documents/.answer: Claude.ai can create Word files when file creation is on. Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code can't without a tool. The DOCX server works in any MCP client: it writes .docx files, fills your own templates and reads existing documents.

/can-claude/make-a-pdf/.intro: Claude.ai can make a PDF with file creation on. Other chat apps need a tool. These are the three PDF jobs people search for most: an invoice PDF, a business document PDF, and editing an existing PDF.
/can-claude/make-a-pdf/.without_tool: In Claude.ai with code execution and file creation turned on, Claude can generate a PDF in its sandbox. In Claude Desktop, Cursor or VS Code without a tool, it gives you text only. In no case does it remember invoice numbers or your business details between chats.
/can-claude/make-a-pdf/.with_tool: Invoice writes numbered A4 invoice PDFs. Billing Docs writes purchase order and credit note PDFs in the same layout. The PDF server merges, splits, stamps and watermarks existing PDFs. Each tool returns the path of the new PDF.

example.prompt: Stamp PAID in green across invoices/INV-0091.pdf, then add my business name and VAT id to the footer of every page.

steps.does: Draws PAID across the pages and writes a new PDF
Adds the business name and VAT id from the shared profile to each footer

example.result: A new copy of INV-0091 stamped PAID with your business footer on every page. The original file is unchanged.

pitfalls: Printing a chat answer to PDF and sending it as an invoice, with no number or VAT id.
Editing a signed PDF in place instead of writing a new copy.
Uploading client PDFs to free online editors.
/can-claude/make-a-pdf/.answer: Claude.ai can make a PDF when file creation is on. In other apps, or for numbered invoices and edits to existing PDFs, connect a server: Invoice writes invoice PDFs, Billing Docs writes order and credit note PDFs, and PDF merges, splits and stamps.

/can-claude/read-zip-files/.intro: Not in most chat apps. And you should check what's inside before you open it. Here's how to list, read and safely unpack a zip from chat.
/can-claude/read-zip-files/.without_tool: Claude.ai with code execution can sometimes unpack an uploaded zip in its sandbox. Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code can't open a .zip without a tool.
/can-claude/read-zip-files/.with_tool: The Zip server lists entries with sizes and ratios, reads one text file from an archive without unpacking, unpacks safely (traversal, absolute-path and symlink entries are refused), creates archives with glob patterns and bundles a month of invoices for your accountant.

example.prompt: List what's inside ~/Downloads/client-records-q3.zip, then show me notes.txt from it without unpacking the rest.

steps.does: Lists every entry with size and compression ratio
Reads notes.txt straight from the archive

example.result: A list of the archive's files and sizes, and the text of notes.txt, with nothing written to disk.

pitfalls: Unpacking an unknown zip straight into your home folder.
Ignoring a huge compression ratio, a sign of a zip bomb.
Emailing a zip of invoices that misses half the month.
/can-claude/read-zip-files/.answer: Most chat apps can't open a zip. Claude.ai with code execution sometimes can. The Zip server lets Claude list entries, read one text file without unpacking, unpack safely with traversal and symlink entries refused, and create new archives with glob patterns. Check the list before you unpack.

/can-chatgpt/create-an-invoice/.intro: ChatGPT writes invoice text well and can make a file with its data analysis tool, but it keeps no numbering or client list. Below is what a connected MCP server adds. We haven't tested the ChatGPT setup, so that part stays unknown.
/can-chatgpt/create-an-invoice/.without_tool: ChatGPT can draft an invoice, do the VAT math and, with its code tool, produce a PDF or spreadsheet file. It doesn't keep a reliable invoice sequence, stored clients or payment status between chats.
/can-chatgpt/create-an-invoice/.with_tool: The Invoice server stores your business profile and clients, numbers each invoice in sequence, writes an A4 PDF and tracks payments and overdue invoices. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers only in some plans and modes. Our setup steps for ChatGPT aren't tested yet, so treat them as unknown.

example.prompt: Invoice Salon Nova for October chair rental, EUR 450, no VAT (small business exemption), due 10 November. Then list my unpaid invoices.

steps.does: Makes the next numbered invoice with one line and no VAT
Writes the A4 PDF
Lists invoices with their status

example.result: A numbered EUR 450 invoice PDF with the due date, and a list of every invoice that's still unpaid.

pitfalls: Restarting at INV-001 in every new chat.
Writing 'no VAT' with no exemption reason when your country requires one.
Assuming every ChatGPT plan can add custom connectors. Check your plan first.
/can-chatgpt/create-an-invoice/.answer: ChatGPT can draft an invoice and make a file, but it keeps no numbering or client list. The Invoice server adds numbered A4 PDFs, stored clients and payment tracking. It works in Claude and Cursor. ChatGPT connector setup is plan-dependent and not tested by us.
